summary.text: Velocity measures both speed and direction, making it a vector quantity that requires magnitude and direction to be defined.
An object maintains a constant velocity only when it travels at a steady speed along a straight line.
An object's average velocity is always less than or equal to its average speed because displacement can decrease while total distance strictly increases.

facts.label: Cause of acceleration
facts.value: change in speed, direction, or both

items.prompt: A car drives around a circular track at a steady speed of 60 km/h. Why is the car considered to be accelerating?

options.label: Its direction of motion changes continuously.
Its overall distance traveled remains constant.
Its speed increases during every lap.
Its engine output fluctuates over time.

items.explain: Even if an object maintains a constant speed, changing its direction of motion means it is undergoing acceleration.

items.prompt: A runner travels 5 kilometers east, turns around, and runs 5 kilometers west back to the starting line. How does their average velocity compare to their average speed?

options.label: Average velocity is greater because speed does not factor in direction.
Average velocity is lower because displacement returned to zero while distance increased.
Average velocity is equal to average speed because movement occurred continuously.
Average velocity cannot be calculated without knowing instantaneous speed.

items.explain: Distance strictly increases during movement, but displacement can decrease back to zero, making average velocity less than or equal to average speed.

items.prompt: On a displacement-time graph for a trip, a straight secant line is drawn between the start time and end time. What does the slope of this line represent?

options.label: The instantaneous speed at the end of the trip.
The total kinetic energy generated during the trip.
The instantaneous velocity at the trip's midpoint.
The average velocity over that time period.

items.explain: The slope of a secant line connecting two time coordinates on a displacement-time graph represents the average velocity across that time frame.

items.prompt: A rocket launches from Earth to travel into deep space. Why is the expression 'escape velocity' scientifically inaccurate?

options.label: The required threshold of about 11,200 m/s depends only on magnitude, not direction.
The required threshold changes depending on whether the rocket travels north or south.
It requires continuous acceleration rather than attaining a specific speed magnitude.
It only applies to objects moving in a circular orbit around Earth.

items.explain: The term is imprecise because reaching a magnitude of about 11,200 m/s leaves Earth's vicinity regardless of direction, making it an escape speed.

items.prompt: Two observers watch a train move along a track. According to Newtonian mechanics, how will non-accelerating observers calculate the train's acceleration?

options.label: They will calculate different acceleration values based on their motion.
All non-accelerating observers will calculate the exact same acceleration values.
Only the stationary observer on the ground can calculate acceleration.
They must use special relativity to agree on acceleration values.

items.explain: In Newtonian mechanics, observers agree on time values, causing all non-accelerating observers to describe an object's acceleration using identical values.

items.prompt: A cyclist’s position changes by 60 metres over a stretch lasting 20 seconds. Which calculation gives the cyclist’s average velocity?

options.label: Multiply 60 metres by 20 seconds
Divide 20 seconds by 60 metres
Divide 60 metres by 20 seconds
Add 60 metres to 20 seconds

items.explain: Average velocity is the change in position divided by the duration of the period, v̄ = Δs/Δt.
